messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: stan hangs with improper posteriors?
parts:
Bob/Matt3:

I don't understand why Stan should hang with improper posteriors. Actually, I ran stan on a model with improper posteriors and it didn't hang. If we have an upper limit on L, Stan should not take too long in the warmup phase, right?

Is there something I'm missing?

A

On Aug 30, 2012, at 5:05 PM, Bob Carpenter wrote:

> On 8/30/12 4:51 PM, Andrew Gelman wrote:
> Improper posteriors should _not_ cause Stan to hang during warmup. Even in warmup we have a limit of 1024 on #leapfrog steps, right? I'd replace that paragraph by the following:
>
> In practice, it effectively hangs. We can call it
> "slow convergence", but to the user it looks like
> it sits there.

messages.author: 1004dd6f66bb10c3
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] stan hangs with improper posteriors?
parts:
It depends on how long a gradient evaluation takes. If each gradient
eval takes 60ms then each iteration could take a minute. If we're only
refreshing the screen every 20 iterations (which I believe is what
happens by default on the command line), then that means the user gets
feedback every 20 minutes, which feels a lot like hanging.

Matt

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] stan hangs with improper posteriors?
parts:
That negative binomial example felt like a lot of
hanging, for instance. Not always, and it could
get to iteration 200 or so of the warmup, but then
it would stall out. (The refresh default is
to have a total of 100 refreshes, which is every 20
iterations if going 2000 iterations.)

- Bob
